_comment: Tunable policy parameters. The review loop edits this file between blocks; policy.py never hardcodes a number that belongs here.
_comment_cycle_cards: Cards cheap enough to burn purely to rotate the hand. ice_golem is deliberately NOT here: it is the Hog's tank, and the guides are explicit that spending it elsewhere guts the push. Without a tank in hand the Hog can only go in naked, which is what block 125 did 37 times for ~0.1 tower damage per match. If the Golem is the only cheap card left, the cycle_any_elixir unblock path below still plays it, but only when we are rich enough that losing it costs nothing.
_comment_cycle_unblock_exclude: Cards the cycle-unblock path may never burn at the back. Musketeer was removed from this list because it being here caused a 10-second dead band (frozen bot) when the hand was exactly the four excluded cards, ending in a bad idle Fireball chip. Cycling a Musketeer at the back at 8.5 elixir is a standard 2.6 proactive play that unblocks the hand.
_comment_fireball_min_value_cost: 4 -> 5 at block 216. This gates only the lone-support-unit branch of the value Fireball (the cluster branch is spell_min_value_elixir and is untouched, as is every defensive Fireball). At 4 a single 4-cost unit - overwhelmingly a Musketeer - drew a 4-elixir Fireball for an even trade that also gave away the deck's answer to a support cluster; `value_fireball_musketeer` fired twice inside one 182s match at block 216. It measures like an even trade too: spell|none|contained fireball is -3.34 over 878 plays, spell|small|contained -4.63 over 82, spell|small -3.76 over 76. Fireball is negative in every bucket it has volume in. Web-verified Aug 2026: the 2.6 guides say to save Fireball as a response, and the June 1 2026 balance update cut its Crown Tower damage 30%% -> 25%% specifically to make passive spell value plays worse. NOTE for whoever tunes this next: the branch admits a cost-4 single either when it is `approaching` (no tower chip, the genuinely bad version) or when it is `on_tower` (4 elixir plus 5.2%% of a tower, which is fine). If Fireball share falls below ~3%%, the better fix is to allow cost-4 singles only when on_tower - that is a small policy.py change - rather than putting this back to 4.
_comment_defend_min_threat: Raised 6.0 -> 8.0 at block 216. 8.0 is exactly the small/medium boundary in experience.threat_bucket, so this makes the gate and the measurement agree: everything the gate now admits lands in `medium` or above. The `defend|small` band (0 < threat < 8) was the worst thing the bot did at volume - musketeer -6.36 over 532 plays, ice_golem -3.34 over 667, cannon -3.12 over 964, skeletons -1.58 over 513, ice_spirit -1.15 over 424, roughly 3100 plays every one of them negative - while the same cards in `defend|medium|contained` run +1.64, +1.56 and +0.21. Web-verified Aug 2026 against the 2.6 guides: Cannon, Musketeer and Fireball are response cards to be held for the opponent's push, not spent on whatever crosses the river. The emergency branch (emergency_min_threat 4.5, emergency_depth 19) is still the backstop, so a 4-8 threat is not ignored - it is answered late, at the tower, and cheaply. If our own towers start bleeding chip from pushes the bot visibly walks past, lower this before touching emergency_min_threat.
_comment_defend_budget: The defensive budget is max(defend_min_budget, threat_elixir * defend_elixir_ratio, threat_score * defend_threat_to_elixir). At ratio 2.0 the bot was licensed to spend twice what the push cost, which inverts the deck's premise - every 2.6 guide describes defence as killing the right thing for the *cheapest* elixir and cycling back to Hog, not killing everything. Measured over blocks 161-163 defence took 48% of all elixir against 28% for pushes, and a single 3-cost Miner drew Cannon, Musketeer and Skeletons (11 elixir) inside five seconds at 0:07. At 1.3 a lone Miner's budget falls to the 4.0 floor - one card, not three - while genuinely big pushes are unaffected because the threat_score term (0.5 per point) then dominates: a 20-threat push still gets 10 elixir. If the bot starts leaking chip damage from cheap two-card pushes, raise the floor before the ratio.
_comment_fallback_min_gap: The last-resort branch fires only when no other rule produced a legal candidate, so it is structurally the play the policy makes when it has run out of ideas - and it measures like it. Over the last 1500 real episodes defend_fallback_skeletons ran -4.48 mean across 35 plays, the worst mean at volume in the whole tag set, and defend_fallback_ice_golem -1.46 across 45; together the family was 66 of the last 600 plays, 11% of everything the bot did, all of it negative. The `vs=` field says why: 32 Barbarians, 26 Goblin pairs and 21 Skeleton pairs drew a fallback, none of which a 1-cost Skeletons drop or a 2-cost Golem beats. At 10s a single push that outlives one gap still draws a second and a third card. 18s is a little over one Cannon lifetime (30s) minus its deploy time, so a push that is genuinely still alive that long can still be answered, while the repeat-dumping stops. If the bot starts taking chip damage from pushes it visibly ignores, lower this before touching emergency_min_threat - that number is pinned to within 0.11 of the Mini P.E.K.K.A. line by test_defends_lone_mini_pekka_at_tower_with_skeletons.
_comment_emergency_min_threat: The floor that separates a push worth spending a last-resort card on from one the tower handles for free. At 3.0 the door opened for three Skeletons (scores 3.53) and a lone Goblin (3.53), and it showed: over the ten clean matches of blocks 176-177, 60 of 161 defend_fallback_* plays fired at threat 3-5 and the `vs=` field on them was overwhelmingly `skeleton,skeleton` - a 2-elixir Ice Golem, the Hog's tank, spent on a card that costs 1. Web-verified: a Crown Tower kills Skeletons outright without taking damage, so any card spent on them is a negative trade by construction. 4.5 is the line the _emergency docstring already describes: a lone Mini P.E.K.K.A. at emergency depth scores 4.61 and a Miner 7.05, so both still open the door, while the Skeleton band no longer does. The margin over the Mini P.E.K.K.A. is only 0.11 - if threat_depth_bonus or the mini_pekka entry in units.json changes, re-check this against test_defends_lone_mini_pekka_at_tower_with_skeletons before assuming it still holds.
_comment_push_reserve: golem_hog gates on elixir >= total_cost + this = 6 + reserve. At 1 the bar was 7, so in the 6-7 band the tanked push was unaffordable and the ladder fell through to a *naked* punish Hog at 4 - strictly the worse play with the tank sitting in hand. Measured over 25 matches only 17 of 108 Hogs went in tanked. At 0 the bar is the push's actual cost; the optional Ice Spirit step is still skipped when unaffordable, and elixir regenerates during the 1s Golem-to-Hog delay.

weights._comment_defend_ranged: Musketeer is the deck's main defensive DPS and its only repeatable air answer, and she is the least-played card in an eight-card deck: 7.4% measured at block 169, 7.8% over the three matches after it, against a 12.5% even share. At 51 she lost the defensive bid to defend_cannon (55) and defend_kite (60) almost every time. 54 keeps her *below* the Cannon, so the 4-3 pull still wins the bid against a ground tank - which is correct and is what test_cannon_answers_a_ground_tank_at_the_4_3_tile pins - while letting her win the ranged-support bids she was narrowly losing. If Cannon share collapses or she starts being played against tanks she cannot solo, put this back to 51.
weights._comment_defend_ranged_216: Back to 51.0 at block 216, which is the value the comment above prescribes for exactly this evidence. The Musketeer is the worst-measuring card in every defensive bucket she has volume in: defend|small -6.36 over 532 plays, defend|small|contained -3.70 over 380, defend|medium -3.38 over 452, defend|medium|contained -1.99 over 417. The raise to 54 was meant to fix her 7.4%% play share, and it did - she is 9.8%% at block 214 - but it bought the share by winning ground-support bids she was losing to the Cannon, and the Cannon measures better in the same situations (defend|medium|contained cannon +0.21 against her -1.99). This only moves the plain ground bid: her air answer is defend_air (62.0) and the anti-Cannon-outranger bid is defend_outranged (75.0), both untouched, so she keeps both roles the deck actually needs her for.

_comment_chip_spare_elixir: Elixir the bar must hold before `_chip` will throw a Fireball at a tower (spellinfo.worth_chipping drops it by 1.0 in double elixir). Lowered 9.5 -> 8.5 on 2026-08-22 (block 206) to close a dead band, not to chip more eagerly. Raising cycle_any_elixir 6.5 -> 9.5 in the previous review left single-elixir ticks around 9 where an all-expensive hand had no generator at all: `_cycle_unblock` needed 9.5, `_chip` needed 9.5, and `_anti_idle` cannot cover it on the tick because it only fires after max_idle_seconds. That is the exact failure bounds.json documents as 278 idle ticks and the user reporting the bot randomly stopping, and it is pinned by test_the_bot_is_never_idle_with_a_full_bar_and_no_threat. 8.5 closes it with the play spellinfo endorses - a Fireball at their tower with nothing on the field to answer - rather than by dumping the Hog's tank behind our king tower. `_chip` still refuses whenever any unit is on the field. If chip Fireballs start costing answers to support clusters, raise this back before touching cycle_any_elixir.
_comment_idle_chip_spells:
Spells the anti-idle filler may throw at a tower rather than leave in hand. the_log is deliberately absent, for the same web-verified reason _chip already excludes it: it deals 13% of its damage to a Crown Tower against Fireball's 25%, off a smaller base, and it is the deck's only answer to a ground swarm. idle_chip_the_log was 116 plays at mean -1.98 over the last 4000 episodes, the worst thing the policy did at volume; the fall-through drops a cheap troop at -1.2 to -1.4 instead and keeps the Log for the next Skeleton Army. If the bot starts visibly idling with a hand of spells, add the_log back before touching max_idle_seconds.

DO NOT empty this key. Tried and reverted twice on 2026-08-22 (block 206), once by the captain and once by the block-206 review agent, which was probably misled by an earlier draft of this very comment. Removing fireball breaks four tests - test_the_bot_is_never_idle_with_a_full_bar_and_no_threat, test_a_long_idle_forces_a_play_even_when_no_generator_fires, test_idle_filler_does_not_burn_the_log_on_chip and test_a_cycled_spell_is_thrown_at_a_tower_not_our_own_back_line - because the Fireball is the *only* outlet the filler has left once the_log is excluded, so emptying this reopens the idle dead band bounds.json records as 278 idle ticks and the user reporting the bot randomly stopping. The chip family does measure badly (-3.73 mean), but the fix is to give the filler a better outlet, not to remove its last one.
